transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-22
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 44 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood SE), James (Aurelia Eng Mgr), Priya (Aurelia ML Eng), Daniel (Aurelia Security), Sara (Aurelia PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): Weekly sync, focused on SDK call stability and structured JSON output. Some noise on timeouts and function-calling non-determinism. Action items agreed.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick note, we've got 44 minutes on the calendar, we'll try to cover the open bugs and the two experiments we discussed last week.
00:18 James: Yep thanks, we only have a little time. Priya has a stacktrace to show from the staging run.
00:26 Priya: yeah so the v2 SDK seemed to behave better overall but we hit repeated function-calling timeouts when the tool chain invoked an external patient-index service. The error looked like a socket timeout but the SDK returned a 502-ish wrapper.
00:45 Ethan: ok can you paste the exact error? sometimes the SDK surfaces a generic gateway error when the runtime cut the connection during KV cache replay. we saw that with long prefixes, it wasn't a pure network failure.
01:02 Priya: (typing) here's snippet — "FunctionCallTimeout: upstream aborted, response truncated" then a following line "internal: streaming reset". sometimes the model returned partial JSON which then fails validation downstream.
01:20 Lena: quick question — are you using the SDK's streaming + function-calling primitive or a non-streamed call? that changes how partial outputs are handled.
01:28 Priya: streaming. we need streaming because the UI shows progressive answers. but streaming + function calling seemed to increase mismatch rates on structured output.
01:40 Maya: that matches what we expected. tradeoff: streaming lowers perceived latency but increases partial-output states, and function calling expects complete, well-formed JSON. one pattern is to buffer until end-of-stream and then validate — but that adds latency.
01:58 James: our acceptance criteria prefer user-perceived latency under 800ms for lookup flows, but also JSON schema stability is critical — can't have malformed diagnoses output.
02:14 Ethan: two quick mitigation ideas: conservative buffer until EOS and then run schema validation, or use a lightweight incremental parser that tolerates partial chunks and only accepts final. The SDK has a sample for incremental validation. we'll share that snippet.
02:30 Priya: could be helpful. also, we saw KV cache thrashing in our tests — keys seemed to be evicted too early when we have different conversation branches, which leads to longer cold starts.
02:46 Ethan: interesting. are you using prefix caching or full KV-state snapshots?
02:50 Priya: prefix caching, default settings. we didn't tune the retention length.
02:58 Lena: ok, tuning the kv-cache retention and the batch window can help cold start. for your traffic pattern (short lookup sequences, many parallel users) we usually suggest a small per-session retention with aggressive early re-warm on expected prefixes. Ethan will drop the recommended config.
03:18 Daniel: quick security question — if we enable KV caching on dedicated, where are the keys stored? do we have KMS/HSM integration?
03:28 Maya: good point. on Redwood Private/ Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via KMS and can integrate with HSM-backed vaults for key material. we also export audit logs with token-level traces if you need for e-discovery. we'll send the SOC2 and KMS integration docs.
03:46 Daniel: perfect. also need to confirm data residency for audit logs — retention 7 years is a must for our compliance team.
03:55 Maya: we'll include retention policy options and cost implications in the doc.
04:05 James: returning to function-calls — we ran a small experiment where the model invoked a chain: fetchPatient -> normalize -> summarize. about 12% resulted in partial JSON from normalize causing downstream failure.
04:22 Ethan: that pattern suggests the tokenizer/windowing is hitting max context on certain prompts. do you have average token lengths?
04:29 Priya: average end-to-end prompt ~1.6k tokens but when we include patient history it spiked.
04:36 Ethan: two levers: shorten system prompt + slot patient history external to model (call with keys), or enable larger sequence models with KV cache tuned. we can suggest quantized weights to cut latency.
04:52 Sara: related question on cost — if we switch to a larger model for those few long requests, how does Redwood recommend routing?
05:00 Maya: smart routing: you can set a policy to route requests over a certain token threshold to a larger model or a dedicated pool. Redwood Optimize recommends this dynamically based on latency/cost targets. we'll add a sample routing rule.
05:18 James: ok. next, we have a reproducible mismatch in structured output where phone numbers are sometimes reformatted and schema validators flag them. is this normalization in the prompt or model side?
05:30 Priya: looks like model-side normalization. we included a tool that post-formats numbers sometimes but the model also changes format inside JSON.
05:38 Lena: for strict contracts we recommend function-calling with explicit argument schema. that prevents model from emitting ad-hoc fields. also lock down the format of fields (regex) in the function spec — SDK will enforce at call boundary.
05:56 Priya: we tried function spec but occasionally the model returned as text not as a function invocation. are there best practices to force function-calls?
06:06 Ethan: yes: 1) make the function the most probable completion by using a short system instruction, 2) use the SDK's function_temperature param low (e.g., 0.0-0.3), 3) provide examples. still not 100% guaranteed but it reduces false negatives.
06:24 James: can you send those example templates?
06:27 Lena: we'll push a set to the shared drive after this call.
06:30 Priya: thanks. another flaky area: when a function chain hits an external API returning 5xx, the SDK retries but sometimes duplicates function calls leading to side-effect duplication.
06:42 Ethan: that's a known edge — idempotency tokens are recommended. Redwood SDK supports an idempotency header on function calls; also we can implement a middleware to dedupe calls at the runtime. we'll sketch a middleware pattern.
06:58 Daniel: that's critical for us — any write operation must be idempotent.
07:03 Maya: noted. action item for Ethan to provide middleware pattern.
07:10 James: ok let's talk benchmarks — we ran 200 lookups average latency 520ms but p95 was 1.9s. baseline on Red API was 420ms p95 1.1s. why the gap?
07:28 Ethan: likely due to batching and cold kv cache. Are you sending many small single-request bursts vs grouped?
07:34 Priya: single-request bursts, real user traffic.
07:38 Ethan: for that pattern we recommend smaller batch windows, e.g., 10-20ms to reduce tail latency. also enabling prefix caching for hot keys helps. We'll share a microbenchmark script.
07:55 Maya: we'll also offer a dedicated test window on our cluster so you can run with warm caches.
08:02 James: appreciate that.
08:06 Maya: quick note — we saw mention of Anthropic & OpenAI in previous threads, any reason you evaluated them?
08:12 Sara: mainly for hallucination profiles and privacy concerns with hosted vendors. Redwood's private option is attractive.
08:18 Maya: good to know.
08:21 Priya: one more small bug: SDK 2.1.4 telemetry isn't showing token-level cost on our end. suspected misconfigured API key scope.
08:31 Ethan: can you check that your API keys include telemetry:read scope? we'll also surface a debug script.
08:39 Priya: will check.
08:42 Maya: ok let's recap next steps — Ethan shares benchmark script and middleware pattern, Maya sends security docs and routing sample, Priya runs staging run and posts results, Daniel shares KMS rotation policy. we agreed on a dedicated test window next Tue 2026-12-30 for two hours.
09:06 James: sounds good. quick scheduling note — can we squeeze a short security-only 30-min call the following week?
09:12 Daniel: yes for sure.
09:15 Maya: perfect, we'll propose times.
09:18 (crosstalk)
09:22 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and the shared drive links. meeting adjourned.
